meanings.note: First-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are'), the most productive verb class in French. Core French verb meaning 'to accept, to agree'.

examples.text: Quand vous regardez des films, des scènes d'amour...
examples.trans: When you watch films, love scenes...

examples.text: Tout le monde en place pour cet après-midi.
examples.trans: Everyone in place for this afternoon.

examples.text: Je veux réussir ma scène cet après-midi.
examples.trans: I want to succeed in my scene this afternoon.

meanings.note: invariable in the plural; cet après-midi = this afternoon

examples.text: Il arrête de travailler à six heures.
Sans toi, je crois que j'arrêterais ce métier.
examples.trans: Without you, I think I'd quit this job.

meanings.note: as a masculine noun: pour le bien de = for the good of
as a masculine noun: pour le bien de = for the good of
à bout = at the end of one's tether, exhausted

examples.trans: At the end of the street.

examples.text: Je suis complètement à bout avec cette histoire.
examples.trans: I am completely exhausted with this story.

meanings.note: before a noun: ce film, cette tête, ces gens
as a pronoun in c'est, ce n'est pas; becomes c' before a vowel

examples.text: Je ne connais rien aux contrats.

meanings.note: dans une heure = in an hour

First-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are'), the most productive verb class in French. Prefix 'dé-'/'des-' (from Latin 'dis-'/'de-') marks reversal, removal, or separation. Core French verb meaning 'to declare, state'.

examples.text: Je déclare ouvert ce grand festival!
examples.trans: I declare open this great festival!
Mr Samuel Kerr has passed away.

meanings.note: formal, official: used by doctors, officials, in letters

examples.trans: You don't stand up for me.

examples.text: Pourquoi te donner dix pour cent si tu ne me défends pas?

meanings.en: to defend, to stand up for

examples.text: Cette scène oblige à se dénuder.

meanings.note: First-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are'), the most productive verb class in French. Prefix 'in-'/'im-' marks negation ('un-, in-') or inward motion. Core French verb meaning 'to indicate, state, point out'.
